name: Beanstalk GovernanceFacet emergencyCommit on unsnapshotted voting power
summary: GovernanceFacet.vote and emergencyCommit read voting power (Roots) at call time with no snapshot or holding period, so Silo deposits made in the same transaction count. The attacker flash-borrowed liquidity, deposited it, voted its own BIP to the two-thirds supermajority and emergency-committed it; the BIP's init delegatecall moved the Silo's assets out.
notes: Victims are the diamond and the BEAN:3CRV, BEAN:LUSD and BEAN:ETH pools whose LP it held almost entirely; the LP tokens are looked through to the non-BEAN assets drained from those pools, so they are not listed separately.

The attack itself crashed BEAN and the attacker never sold the BEAN it kept, so BEAN is valued at what it realised, nothing (rule 15). Aave premiums, slippage and the USDC donation came out of the drained assets and are not subtracted.
Later diamond cuts before the exploit replaced other facets (BDV functions, LUSD whitelisting) but not the governance selectors; the attacker's supermajority did not depend on them.
